goal: Review Python code for correctness, typing, resource handling, security pitfalls and tests.
use: Review Python code for correctness, typing, resource handling, security pitfalls and tests. Use when asked to review or harden a Python project or module.

steps.note: Read the project setup. Open pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, requirements files and lint configuration.
Check correctness. Look for mutable default arguments, late-binding closures, bare `except:`, swallowed exceptions, `is` comparisons with literals, and integer versus float division.
Check resources. Files, sockets and database connections must be closed, normally through `with`.

Check security. Flag `eval` and `exec` on input, `pickle` on untrusted data, `subprocess` with `shell=True` or built strings, unsafe YAML loading, paths joined from user input, and SQL built with f-strings.
Check typing and the public API. Public functions need correct annotations.
Check tests. Find branches and public functions with no test, and assertions that cannot fail.

protocol.title: Read the project setup
protocol.text: Open pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, requirements files and lint configuration. Note the Python version the project targets.

protocol.title: Check correctness
protocol.text: Look for mutable default arguments, late-binding closures, bare `except:`, swallowed exceptions, `is` comparisons with literals, and integer versus float division.

protocol.title: Check resources
protocol.text: Files, sockets and database connections must be closed, normally through `with`. Note generators and threads that are never joined.

protocol.title: Check security
protocol.text: Flag `eval` and `exec` on input, `pickle` on untrusted data, `subprocess` with `shell=True` or built strings, unsafe YAML loading, paths joined from user input, and SQL built with f-strings.

protocol.title: Check typing and the public API
protocol.text: Public functions need correct annotations. Flag `Any` that leaks out, and `Optional` values used without a None check.

protocol.title: Check tests
protocol.text: Find branches and public functions with no test, and assertions that cannot fail.

protocol.title: Report
protocol.text: List each finding as `file:line`, with severity (high, medium or low), the problem and the fix. Mark what you did not run.
